title: Card index
what: Exactly the locked content: the head, the title and rows 01–06, nothing added. The form adds only physical parts of a card box: a guide card for the head, a tab on each card carrying its number and kind badge, card thickness and faint ruling, two box walls and a front panel with a finger notch.
why: A card index is a collection that grows one card at a time and that anyone can add to, which is what an open, community-built Standard is. Rows 01–05 are cards already filed by practitioners; row 06 is the empty divider at the front of the box, rimmed in orange, kept for your card.
how: CSS 3D: cards stand one in front of the other, each a few px further forward in Z, so each shows its top strip and its tab, staggered left, centre and right like real index tabs. The side wall is an SVG plane turned into depth, and the front panel sits in front of everything. On load the box rises, the guide card drops in, then cards 01–06 drop in one by one (ease-out, about 1.2s). The base pointer tilt still works, and 06 lifts and fills faintly orange on hover or focus. Reduced motion shows everything at its final state; on mobile the box is flat and seen straight on, with tabs and overlap kept and a 129px tap target on 06.
